newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey Bursa Cement sees 30 pct rise in '97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turkey Bursa Cement sees 30 pct rise in '97 sales.

text.p: Turkish cement producer Bursa Cimento Fabrikasi A.S. aims to increase sales by 30 percent to 1.63 million tonnes next year, a senior company official said.
The company's total sales, 927,000 tones in the first nine months of this year, are expected to stand at 1.25 million tonnes at end-1996, general manager Burhan Evcil told Reuters.
Bursa Cimento completed a 1.8 trillion-lira investment in June to increase its production capacity by 50 percent to 1.8 million tonnes. It is now Turkey's eighth biggest cement producer.
The company's shares are traded on the Istanbul Stock Exchange. Bursa Cimento shares opened unchanged at 12,250 lira on Tuesday.
Evcil said the company would continue investing in capacity expansion and modernisation projects, such as increasing the capacity of cement mills and modernisation of clinker ovens.

"Our production capacity has become equal to the milling capacity since our investment was completed," he said. "But cement production needs higher milling capacity. So we will start a new investment in 1997 to increase our milling capacity. The investment will be completed in 1998."
The company's nine month sales were realised in the buoyant domestic market. Evcil said his firm had been exporting cement to Belgium and sevreal west and north African states since October.
He expects exports to reach 50,000 tonnes or $2 million by the end of the year.
Bursa Cimento set its 1997 exprot targets at 250,000 tonnes for cement and 50,000 tones for clinker, both worth a total of $10 million.
Evcil said Bursa's target market is domestic consumers.
The company has a four percent market share in Turkey and 12 percent in the Marmara region.
